leagues.notes:
Method: 40+ WebSearch queries. WebFetch was unavailable, and the WebSearch tool hands back summarized result text, not raw page text. So each snippet is the closest verbatim sentence or fragment the search output quoted for that source. Some snippets (Thompson, Gusta and Metcalf bio fragments, Jeanty rushYards) are short quoted fragments, not full sentences. For a few facts I can't be sure which listed URL the quoted sentence came from: the Sonny Styles "At 6-foot-5 and 244 lbs..." sentence (filed under NFL.com; could be Commanders.com or Fox Sports), the Paea and Wake CBS Sports lines, the Calvin Johnson draft line (SI), and Worthy's 1.49 split (Burnt Orange Nation). Check those before display.

NOT FOUND: (1) A full-season final Next Gen Stats fastest-ball-carrier leader for 2024 or 2025. I only found in-season snapshots: Turpin 22.36 mph was the 2024 leader as of Week 11, and Jonathan Taylor 22.38 mph was the 2025 leader as of Week 10. A faster run may have come later in either season. (2) A 2025 broken-tackles leader. Sources only give "missed tackles forced", a different stat (PFF has Kenneth Walker III at 86), so I recorded no brokenTackles facts. (3) Combine-measured weight for Chris Johnson. The 197 lb figure could not be confirmed, so I used Wikipedia's listed 5-11/203. (4) Paea's combine-measured height/weight. I used RotoWire's draft-workout figures, 6-1/300; Wikipedia lists 295. (5) An undrafted player with elite testing who is currently an NFL starter. The only undrafted entry is the legend Cameron Wake.

CONFLICTS: Worthy's combine top speed is 24.41 mph (Yahoo/NFL tweet), but AOL and SJV Sun say 24.21 and NBC says 24.42. His 10-yard split is 1.49 in most sources, 1.45 in some. CBS's same-day table showed his 40 as 4.22 before the official 4.21. Vernon Davis's TE 40 is 4.40 per NFL.com (recorded, as most official), but other sources give 4.38 or 4.39; the Jets site says timing glitches were possible in 2006. That is why NFL.com calls Sadiq's 4.39 a TE record. Sadiq weighed 241 at the combine; Oregon and RotoWire list 245. His vertical is 43 per The Ringer and 43.5 per other trackers, so I left it out. Sonny Styles' 43.5 vertical is called the LB record by NFL.com, but another source ranks it second behind Cameron Wake's 45.5 (Wake tested as a Penn State LB). Lorenzo Styles is called a safety by the CFP recap and a cornerback by Buckeye Sports. Paea's 49 reps is the official record, but Justin Ernest reportedly did 51 in 1999 (undrafted, never played). Metcalf's body fat is 1.9% (SI, ESPN) or 1.6% (CBS, USA Today), and CBS called his 4.33 unofficial at the time. Woolen's combine weight is 205, while Seahawks.com later said 210. His arms are 33 5/8 in most sources, but SI says 33.5 and a Seattle outlet says 34. His 40 is ranked tied-fourth (ESPN) or tied-third (current Wikipedia). Brenen Thompson's height and weight vary on fantasy sites; I used combine/Mockdraftable figures. Jeanty's 863 yards after contact (Raiders.com, citing NGS) conflicts with SumerSports' 351, which looks like a partial count. Raiders.com is the more official source. Byron Jones' weight is 194 (Wikipedia) or 196 (UConn-era profile). Gusta's weight is 316 (BC Lions) or 308 (3DownNation).

STATUS/TEAM CAVEATS: The sources confirm these 2026 teams: Worthy (Chiefs), Turpin (Cowboys), Taylor (Colts), Metcalf (Steelers), Woolen (Eagles, 1-year deal March 2026), and the 2026 rookies Thompson (Chargers), Sadiq (Jets), Sonny Styles (Commanders), Lorenzo Styles Jr. (Saints) and Stowers (Eagles; RotoWire lists him on IR with a hamstring injury). For Jeanty, the Raiders are the team named in 2025-season sources; I found no explicit 2026 roster confirmation. Tyreek Hill was released by Miami in Feb 2026 and was an unsigned free agent as of late-Aug 2026 reports; no later signing was found. David Gusta led the 2026 combine with 37 bench reps but signed with the CFL's BC Lions on 2026-04-27, right after the draft. No source explicitly says "undrafted". He sits under status free-agent only because the enum has no CFL option; drop him if CFL players are out of scope. Legend status: Calvin Johnson's retirement (after 2015) and Sensabaugh's (one-day contract with Dallas) are confirmed in results. For Byron Jones (last played for Miami, 2020-2022), Cameron Wake (no NFL games since 2019; his agent denied a 2020 retirement report), Paea, Vernon Davis and Chris Johnson, the results showed no explicit retirement announcement. Their "Retired"/legend tags are an inference from inactivity, not a sourced fact.

OTHER: Tyreek Hill's 23.24 mph (2016) is in-game Next Gen Stats data. Worthy's 24.41 mph was measured on a combine drill, so the two are not comparable. Rank wording for Brenen Thompson ("third-fastest receiver to run at the combine since 2003", tying Jerome Mathis' 4.26 in 2005) appeared in a result whose exact URL I couldn't pin down, so his rankClaim is empty.

- Witt 2024 sprint speed: B-Ref and Yahoo say 30.5 ft/s, Sportsnaut says 30.4. Witt's weight: ESPN and Topps say 200 lb, B-Ref says 185 lb.

leagues.notes:
I ran about 49 searches before the shared web-search budget for this turn ran out. Two attribution-check searches, for Cedric Coward's wingspan quote and Cameron Boozer's numbers, did not run. WebFetch was not used.

HOW THE SNIPPETS WERE CAPTURED: The search tool returns summarized excerpts, not raw page text. Each snippet is the excerpt text exactly as the search result showed it, and some are partly paraphrased by the tool. For a few facts the outlet is a best match among the links the result listed: Cameron Boozer's and AJ Dybantsa's measurement line (College Football Network), Boozer's No. 3 pick (AP via AM800), Cameron Carr's NBA.com height and wingspan, and Drake Powell's 200.4-lb weight (NBADraft.net). These should be spot-checked before display.

LEFT OUT: Cedric Coward (7'2.25" wingspan, largest among guards at the 2025 combine) because I could not tell which outlet the quote came from, and sources disagree on his height (6'5" vs 6'6"). Also Darryn Peterson (No. 2 pick, Utah), whose measurements were not standout. Morez Johnson Jr. (39" max vertical, 6'9" barefoot, 9.5" hands) because his draft slot was not confirmed. Jayden Quaintance (11-inch hand width, tied for the 2026 combine lead) because his draft status was unknown. Kenny Gregory (45.5", 2001) and Jericho Sims (44.5", 2021) appear on NBA.com's all-time vertical list but were not profiled.

NOT FOUND: No 2025-26 NBA tracking average-speed leaderboard. The only speed figure is Andre Jackson Jr. at 4.83 mph in 2024-25, from a RotoWire team-by-team article hosted on an unusual rotowire subdomain. No verified all-time lane-agility record turned up. Zach LaVine's 10.42 (2014) is the lowest time I saw but is not claimed as a record. No official 2026 combine leaderboard or best 2026 three-quarter sprint time was found: No Ceilings named Darius Acuff Jr. best of the day without a number, and a 3.07 for Kingston Flemings was not confirmed. No hand measurements turned up for the profiled players.

CONFLICTS:
- 2026 max vertical leader: one outlet said Dybantsa had the highest (42.0"), but Tobi Lawal (45.5") and Cameron Carr (42.5", ranked No. 2) were both higher. I recorded Lawal's 45.5 from Virginia Tech and NBADraft.net. Roundtable calls it tied for the second-highest mark in combine history, which matches NBA.com's list (Kenny Gregory, 45.5", 2001).
- Lawal standing vertical: 40" (NBADraft.net and Roundtable, which says it led the class) vs 40.5" (Techsideline, which calls it second-highest ever). I recorded 40. Virginia Tech's 49.5" figure comes from pre-draft testing at VCU, not the combine. Bleacher Report does not say whether its 6'7.25" height for Lawal was barefoot.
- Cameron Carr lane agility: one Bleacher Report scouting report says 10.46 was second-fastest, while a Bleacher Report winners/losers piece says Carr had the fastest. His wingspan is 7'0" per NBA.com and NBADraft.net but 7'0.75" per Bleacher Report. I recorded 7'0".
- Dybantsa: wingspan 7'0.25" (most outlets) vs 7'0.5" (CBS Sports and Hoops HQ). Standing vertical 35.5" (NBA.com via Fadeaway World) vs 33.5" (Nordot). Weight 217 lb vs 220 lb (Hoops HQ). His 25.6 points per game is from his BYU college season, not the NBA.
- Kingston Flemings 40.5" max vertical: Bleacher Report ranks it No. 3 among guards, while Sotheby's lists it as third overall.
- Aday Mara 9'9" standing reach: Sotheby's says it ties Mark Williams for second all-time. Larry Brown Sports and other outlets say second behind Tacko Fall.
- Mo Bamba: standing reach 9'7.5" (most sources) vs 9'9" (Richmond Free Press). Height 6'11.25" without shoes (Richmond Free Press) vs "just shy of 7 feet" (CBS Sports). His 2018 wingspan record was later passed by Tacko Fall in 2019.
- Reed Sheppard: most sources say his 42" tied for best at the 2024 combine, but one report ranks it fourth-best. His draft pick number did not appear in any result, so it was not recorded.
- Keon Johnson: his 6-4.75 height was measured in shoes, so it was not recorded as barefoot height.
- Derrick Rose: the 2008 numbers come from the Orlando Pre-Draft Camp (DraftExpress). Rush the Court says his vertical and sprint both ranked third-best at that camp.
- Nate Robinson's 43.5" comes from the 2004 combine table (he withdrew from that draft and was drafted in 2005). His retirement year was not stated in any result, but sources describe a completed 11-season NBA career.
- Andre Jackson Jr.'s height and weight are ESPN roster listings, not barefoot combine measurements.

TEAMS AND STATUS:
